subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should this iMessage sender repair be adopted after canonical handle normalization and live proof, or should the branch pause until the remaining root cause is clarified?
rationale: The repaired sender becomes the identity used for iMessage authorization, pairing, session routing, and reply targeting, so accepting a fallback rule is a security and delivery boundary choice rather than ordinary cleanup.

options.title: Fix normalization and prove live behavior
options.body: Require canonical handle comparisons, focused regression coverage, and redacted after-fix iMessage proof before merge.

options.title: Accept source-only identity risk
options.body: Merge based on source review and pre-fix incident evidence while maintainers own the remaining live-payload uncertainty.

options.title: Pause for a narrower root cause
options.body: Leave or close the draft branch after a clearer iMessage failure report identifies whether a different fix is needed.

recommendation.title: Fix normalization and prove live behavior
recommendation.body: Require canonical handle comparisons, focused regression coverage, and redacted after-fix iMessage proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest recent history across iMessage inbound-processing, target normalization, and channel access boundaries touched by the decision.
